decisions.question: Should WS8 (collapse the 28 agent-facing MCP tools to CLI) land in this issue, or be split to a follow-up after the core event-pump is proven?

options.label: Land WS8 in this issue (collapses prompt + action surface in one pass; larger blast radius but more deletion)
Split WS8 to a follow-up (smaller core change; ships event-pump first, MCP collapse after the new control flow is validated in production)

Land WS8 partially in this issue (only the net-new CLI commands needed by WS3 — get-state, list-blocking, get-context — and the deletion of MCP tools with existing CLI parity; defer prose-bearing propose/ack/nack collapse to a follow-up so the #2741 stdin/file-path rule can be designed separately)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Split the MCP→CLI collapse to a SEPARATE follow-up issue — specifically the deletion of the 28 agent-facing MCP tools and the prose-bearing propose/ack/nack CLI migration (with the #2741 stdin/file-path rule) all go to the follow-up. HOWEVER, this issue MUST build any net-new CLI commands the new wait-loop / event-pump depends on (e.g. brc get-state, brc list-blocking, phase get-context, and any other tool the per-event handler invokes) so the new control flow has full CLI coverage for everything it needs. Do NOT delete the existing MCP tools in this issue — just guarantee CLI availability for the event-pump's needs; the actual collapse/deletion of the MCP surface is the follow-up issue's scope."}

decisions.question: If the WS0 spike shows the Qwen-route provider cache TTL is materially worse than the Anthropic route, how should v1 ship?

options.label: Ship v1 with the Qwen route enabled and a keep-warm loop sized to the measured provider-cache TTL (full route parity at the cost of a recurring keep-warm token spend)

Ship v1 with the Qwen route gated off behind a per-route flag (Anthropic route gets the durable fix immediately; Qwen route stays on the old capped-restart path until keep-warm or a provider TTL change makes it economical)

Block v1 on Qwen-route cache validation (no ship until the Qwen route's per-event cost is within the operator's per-cycle budget; treat the Anthropic route's measured-clear status as not enough to justify a partial rollout)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Ship v1 with the Qwen route ENABLED on the new event-pump (do NOT gate it onto the old capped-restart path — that path is being deleted per cq-4). Operator has confirmed both the Anthropic and Qwen routes have a free cache TTL > 5 minutes (Anthropic measured at 1h in WS7). Therefore: do NOT build a keep-warm / cache-refresh loop for v1. WS0 must instrument the actual per-event cold-read / cache-creation cost on the Qwen route across a realistic worst-case BRC idle (specifically a reviewer parked while a producer addresses a NACK and re-proposes — observed ~7-8 min in practice). ONLY if that measured cold-read waste proves material should a BOUNDED keep-warm be added, and then: Qwen-route only, active only during idles approaching the TTL, with a capped total number of refreshes, and SUPPRESSED during HITL / awaiting-human waits (which can last hours and would otherwise burn tokens keeping a cache warm for an event that is hours away). Never add keep-warm on the Anthropic route (1h TTL makes it unnecessary). Rationale: Qwen token costs are low, so worst-case cold-read waste is at most a few cents per occurrence; a speculative background refresh loop adds exactly the kind of stateful liveness mechanism this issue is trying to delete."}

decisions.question: What is the desired terminal state when the new safety budget (replacing the 3-restart FAIL cap) is exhausted?

options.label: OVERSEER_ALERT + HITL decision (current behaviour preserved: operator picks resume/abort, no automatic FAIL)
OVERSEER_ALERT only; pipeline keeps running indefinitely (operator must intervene to stop it; suits the 'no-progress' interpretation where there is nothing wrong, just nothing happening)
Hard FAIL after a configurable wall-clock cap (preserves the #2806 'producer permanent death → FAILED' semantics but on time rather than restart count)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "OVERSEER_ALERT + HITL decision (current behaviour preserved: operator picks resume/abort, no automatic FAIL). HARD REQUIREMENT (operator-added): because the old capped-restart wrapper is being deleted entirely (cq-4), this no-progress safety budget is now the ONLY safety net, so it must be robust to SDLC-host failure. The parked HITL decision AND the safety-budget / no-progress state must be persisted DURABLY SERVER-SIDE (in the orchestrator), not held only in the host process driving the pipeline. If the host running the SDLC pipeline dies, a restarted host must be able to resume the awaiting-human decision and the budget state rather than losing them. Treat host-death recoverability as a requirement of this decision, not a nice-to-have."}

decisions.question: How long should the old capped-restart wrapper path be retained behind a flag after the new event-pump path lands?

options.label: Until the next release tag, then delete (forcing-function for full migration; smallest carrying cost)
Until N successful pipelines complete on the new path (e.g. 50) without any new restart-related alerts, then delete (data-driven)
Indefinitely as a configurable opt-out (operator can always escape-hatch to the legacy path; largest carrying cost but lowest risk)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Delete the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely — do NOT retain it behind a flag. Operator decision: the event-pump replaces it outright; there is no flagged fallback to the old MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS=3 / restart-and-FAIL behaviour. (Note the interaction the operator flagged: because the old path is gone, the Qwen route cannot 'fall back to the old path' — see cq-2, which ships Qwen on the new event-pump directly. And the new no-progress safety budget from cq-3 is therefore the sole safety net, with its durable-server-side-state requirement.) This overrides the canned options, all of which assumed retaining the old path for some duration."}

questions.question: Are there operator-side budget caps (per-pipeline token spend, per-event wall-clock, keep-warm-loop $/hour) that should be expressed as hard fail conditions for the WS0 spike rather than just instrumentation? If yes, name the threshold.

Is the new memory artifact (.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md) considered authoritative audit material that must be preserved post-pipeline, or ephemeral coordination state that can be cleaned up with the pod? (Affects retention policy and gateway treatment.)

Are there operator-side budget caps (per-pipeline token spend, per-event wall-clock, keep-warm-loop $/hour) that should be expressed as hard fail conditions for the WS0 spike rather than just instrumentation? If yes, name the threshold.
questions.answer: Instrument only, no hard caps. WS0 should measure and report per-pipeline token spend, per-event wall-clock, and (if ever built) keep-warm-loop $/hour, but nothing should auto-fail on a fixed threshold; the operator will judge go/no-go from the reported numbers. Note: the operator has confirmed both routes have a free cache TTL > 5 min, so the Qwen-route cache risk that motivated tight caps is substantially de-risked.

questions.question: Is the new memory artifact (.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md) considered authoritative audit material that must be preserved post-pipeline, or ephemeral coordination state that can be cleaned up with the pod? (Affects retention policy and gateway treatment.)
questions.answer: Ephemeral coordination state — brc-memory.md can be cleaned up with the pod; the orchestrator message history is the durable reconstruction backstop. HARD CAVEAT: this is acceptable ONLY because recovery must NOT depend on the ephemeral memory file surviving. Pipeline/host recovery (see cq-3) must work from durable server-side orchestrator state + message history alone. If during implementation the brc-memory.md file turns out to be load-bearing for correct recovery after a host or pod restart, revisit this answer and make the artifact durable instead of ephemeral.
